own_solution.law: For an initially uncharged capacitor, VC(t) = V0[1 - exp(-t/(R_total C))]. The base time constant is (5000 Ω)(20 × 10^-6 F) = 0.100 s, giving VC(0.080 s) = 6.60805243 V. An added series resistance q changes R_total to R + q.
assumptions: The battery, resistors, wires and capacitor are ideal, and the capacitor does not leak.
Each added series resistor is present from the initial connection.
Opening the charging circuit leaves no discharge path through the capacitor.

TABC4.regime: The opening time q exceeds the observation time: q > 80 ms.

T2215.regime: The disconnection time q exceeds the observation time: q > 80 ms.

defect_reasons.failed_transformation_identity: For both relevant resistor sentences, the certified answers contradict the stated replacement R_total = R + q in the charging time constant.
defect_reasons.relevant_variable_removed_from_equation: The certified answers for TD742 and T5A17 omit the effect of the added series resistance and incorrectly repeat the base answer at every q.

notes: The pass-1 physics and assignments stand. The pass-2 verdict changes because the newly supplied certified answers for both relevant resistor sentences are wrong. The governing RC relations and series-resistance wiring are correct when evaluated with consistent units. The base answer, disconnected-resistor answers, and all switching answers at 300, 500 and 1000 ms are correct. For opening before observation, the capacitor retains V0[1 - exp(-q/tau)] under the stated ideal conditions. The paired sentences preserve the intended numbers and units. The numerical failures are substantive, not rounding errors.
